pharm: Long-acting selective serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist that blocks serotonin-mediated activation of the vomiting reflex, preventing chemotherapy- and surgery-induced nausea and vomiting.
quick: CINV: 0.25 mg IV once, ~30 min before chemotherapy; PONV: 0.075 mg IV once before anesthesia induction
Parenteral; not affected by food (oral formulation taken with/without food)
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
Caution; unknown if present in human milk
Hypersensitivity, serotonin syndrome, ECG/QT in at-risk patients
summary: Palonosetron is a second-generation, long-acting selective 5-HT3 receptor antagonist used to prevent acute and delayed nausea and vomiting from moderately emetogenic chemotherapy, acute nausea/vomiting from highly emetogenic chemotherapy, and postoperative nausea and vomiting. The usual adult dose is a single 0.25 mg IV dose about 30 minutes before chemotherapy (0.075 mg IV before anesthesia induction for PONV). Its prolonged half-life allows single-dose protection over the delayed phase. It is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity, and serotonin syndrome can occur, especially with concomitant serotonergic drugs.
indications: Prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with moderately emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (MEC) in adults
Prevention of acute nausea and vomiting associated with highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy (HEC) in adults
Prevention of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) for up to 24 hours following surgery in adults
Prevention of acute nausea and vomiting associated with emetogenic chemotherapy (including HEC) in pediatric patients 1 month to less than 17 years

dosage.d: 0.25 mg as a single dose, infused over 30 seconds, beginning ~30 minutes before chemotherapy
dosage.n: Oral formulation 0.5 mg ~1 hour before chemotherapy is an alternative

dosage.d: 20 mcg/kg (maximum 1.5 mg) as a single dose, infused over 15 minutes, ~30 minutes before chemotherapy
dosage.n: Note different dosing units in pediatrics

dosage.d: 0.075 mg as a single dose over 10 seconds immediately before induction of anesthesia

admin: Administer as a single intravenous dose; for CINV infuse over 30 seconds ~30 minutes before chemotherapy
For PONV, give 0.075 mg IV over 10 seconds immediately before induction of anesthesia
Flush the IV line with normal saline before and after administration
Inspect for particulate matter and discoloration before use; do not mix with other drugs
moa: Palonosetron is a selective serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist with strong binding affinity for the 5-HT3 receptor and little affinity for other receptors. Chemotherapy releases serotonin from enterochromaffin cells of the small intestine, which activates 5-HT3 receptors on vagal afferents and in the chemoreceptor trigger zone of the area postrema, triggering the vomiting reflex. By blocking these receptors peripherally and centrally, palonosetron prevents nausea and vomiting. Its high affinity and long half-life provide sustained antiemetic protection.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to palonosetron or any of its components
relative: Known hypersensitivity to other 5-HT3 receptor antagonists (cross-reactivity possible)
Conditions or drugs that prolong the QT interval
monitor: ECG/QT interval in patients with risk factors or electrolyte abnormalities

preg: There are limited human data on palonosetron use in pregnancy; animal studies did not show clear adverse developmental effects at clinical exposures. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether palonosetron is present in human milk. Because of the lack of data, consider the benefits of breastfeeding along with the mother's clinical need and potential effects on the infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is necessary for patients with renal impairment, including severe impairment, as renal impairment does not significantly affect total body clearance.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is necessary for patients with hepatic impairment.

major: Serotonergic drugs (SSRIs, SNRIs, MAO inhibitors, triptans, mirtazapine, fentanyl, tramadol, methylene blue) - increased risk of serotonin syndrome
QT-prolonging drugs - additive QT prolongation risk
moderate: Other 5-HT3 antagonists - no added benefit and possible additive effects
minor: Palonosetron has low potential for CYP-mediated drug interactions at clinical doses
interactions.food: Parenteral administration is unaffected by food; oral palonosetron may be taken with or without food.
interactions.diagnostics: May contribute to QT-interval changes; obtain baseline ECG in patients with cardiac risk factors or electrolyte disturbances.

serious: Hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis and anaphylactic shock
emergency: Serotonin syndrome (agitation, hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Signs of hypersensitivity during and after administration
Symptoms of serotonin syndrome, especially when combined with serotonergic agents
ECG/QT interval in patients with congenital long QT, electrolyte abnormalities, or other QT-prolonging drugs
Antiemetic efficacy across the acute and delayed phases
counsel: This medicine is given as an injection to prevent nausea and vomiting from chemotherapy or surgery
Tell your care team if you have ever reacted to ondansetron, granisetron, or similar antiemetics
Report agitation, fast heartbeat, fever, muscle stiffness, sweating, or confusion - signs of serotonin syndrome
Constipation and headache are common; report severe or persistent symptoms
Tell your team about all medicines, especially antidepressants and migraine medicines
pk: Antiemetic effect develops shortly after IV administration
Peak plasma concentration reached rapidly after IV dose
Single dose protects through the acute and delayed phases (up to ~5 days)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C; protect from light, do not freeze
pearls: Second-generation 5-HT3 antagonist with a ~40 hour half-life - single dose covers delayed CINV without repeat dosing
No renal or hepatic dose adjustment required
Serotonin syndrome can occur, particularly with SSRIs/SNRIs, MAOIs, triptans, fentanyl, tramadol
Cross-hypersensitivity with other setrons is possible - do not rechallenge after a hypersensitivity reaction
Often combined with dexamethasone (and an NK1 antagonist for HEC) per antiemetic guidelines
missed: Palonosetron is given as a single dose before chemotherapy or surgery rather than on a daily schedule, so a missed-dose schedule does not apply; if a planned pre-treatment dose is missed, contact the care team for guidance before the emetogenic exposure.
overdose: There is no known antidote to palonosetron; overdose should be managed with supportive care. Because of its large volume of distribution, dialysis is unlikely to be effective. In animals, high lethal doses produced convulsions, gasping, pallor, cyanosis, and collapse.
